title: A cover with an adjustable budget
promptMarkdown: Let $A\subset\mathbb R$ be countable. Prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$ it lies in an open set $O$ with $m(O)<\varepsilon$. Does the same conclusion hold for every set with outer measure zero? Explain using the definition, not a named regularity theorem.
hintLadder: Assign a summable fraction of the total budget to each point.
For the second assertion, unpack the meaning of infimum zero.
